method: Off/on/on/off; same opt-in prototype server and client. 16 drags per rate/version; three simultaneous viewers per drag. Stages overlap. All successful samples retained, including cold first moves.

trials.method: Eight real Legacy player drags per CPU rate, with simultaneous 2D and 3D DM clients in Player visibility. All assisted, same disposable courtyard and same server/client build with mask separation toggled off/on. 140 monsters, 48 fixed lights, 28 wall segments, carried lantern, heavy darkness and remembered terrain. All three browser CPUs throttled after startup; unrestricted server on same host. Legacy WebGL blocked, standard modes real GPU, Low. Missing LFS models use test stand-ins. No video/trace, WAN latency, RAM or GPU restriction. First-paint estimate uses two RAF opportunities. Server stages overlap.

status: Do not enable: first-motion latency regressed in all measured conditions; Legacy regular-darkness/daylight visual acceptance failed.
scope: Integrated server image preparation, transport, decode, Legacy CSS color composition and 2D/3D GPU mask composition.
Three simultaneous viewers with server assist enabled; separation off/on on the same server/client source.
64 drags, 192 viewer observations. 16 observations per condition and viewer.
No live app/server updates. Disposable databases and isolated port 4179.
limitations: CPU slowdown applied after startup; no initial-load CPU benchmark.
5090 GPU for standard modes, WebGL blocked for Legacy. This does not emulate an old integrated GPU.
No WAN latency, bandwidth limit, RAM cap, recording, or browser trace.
Test stand-in figures replace unavailable LFS models.
Current standard path retains DOM fallback mask updates; this is not the minimum possible client workload.
Movement testing and targeted visual comparisons do not certify every spell effect or the entire application UI.
interpretation: This prototype trades Legacy bandwidth for additional image preparation latency.
Standard modes gain large animation mask downloads and must wait for server-prepared frames.
Do not generalize these results into proof that every server-mask architecture must be slower.
Further candidates: reuse static lamp coverage across poses; send each mode only the image channels it consumes; avoid redundant local fallback work once safe; evaluate small changed-region updates.

visualAcceptance.threshold: Mean absolute RGB difference below 1 on 0..255 scale and fewer than 1 percent of pixels with any channel difference over 12.
visualAcceptance.result: 2D and 3D passed after real pan/zoom; Legacy failed regular darkness and daylight.
visualAcceptance.initialViewLimitation: 2D regular-darkness initial capture was inconsistent. A fresh camera render resolved the large difference; startup visual parity remains unverified.

validation.movement: All four paired trials passed (64 drags, 192 viewer observations); Legacy pose/alignment checks included.
validation.visual: 2 passed, 1 failed in explicit acceptance run.
validation.unit: 2440 tests passed across 249 files (221.61 seconds). Includes the separated-mask channel, reconstruction, per-viewer grant and shared-image-job tests.

bandwidthNote: renderTransferBytes uses Resource Timing transferSize (including headers, excluding browser-cache body bytes); renderImageBytes uses encodedBodySize and also counts cached bodies. Only render-asset requests are counted, not socket state messages.
